working_definition: Lawf1 (lamina wide-field neuron 1) is an optic-lobe interneuron with wide-field arborisations spanning multiple lamina cartridges, distinct from the columnar lamina monopolar (L1-L5) and centrifugal (C2/C3) neurons. It was identified directly at res-2.0 using eya and hth co-expression without Lim1, distinguishing it from its sister type Lawf2 (Chen et al., 2016).

best_match.fbbt_definition: A lamina wide-field neuron that has a main projection that ascends via the first optic chiasm into the lamina where it is restricted to a single column for most of its length before making wide-field arborizations in the distal lamina. These neurons also arborize on the distal surface of the medulla in a circular field of about 20 columns. Several linking fibers from this arborization descend into M4 where they form a wide arborization field covering about 30-40 columns (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Morante and Desplan, 2008). In the lamina, it forms numerous presynaptic connections to lamina monopolar neuron L3 and lamina intrinsic (amacrine) neuron (Rivera-Alba et al., 2011).

justification: FBbt:00003741 is the classical Fischbach and Dittrich (1989)/Morante and Desplan (2008) lamina wide-field neuron 1, matching the report's Lawf1 (wide-field arborisation spanning multiple cartridges, distinct from columnar L-neurons). The paper's own eya/hth (no Lim1) marker call for Lawf1 (Chen et al., 2016) is the modern molecular identification of this same classical morphological type. Label provenance is clean (GEO = Table S2, no REVIEW flag, no subclustering performed), and this is an adult brain atlas for which the mature adult form is appropriate.
recommendation: Accept as exact match at high confidence.
